confirm.text: Jobe selected "Stop work authority was discussed" and did not select "Unsafe conditions". This is the inverse of the usual pattern: the narrative names a specific hazard that was intervened on, while the multi-select does not reflect it. Follow-up: confirm whether stop-work authority was in fact exercised here, and reinforce that a condition like this should be selected.
3. Michael Jobe (job 36225, 07:16 AM) and Robert Henigan (job 36226, 07:17 AM) — XTO, McClintic A 8H. Both jobs were cancelled on arrival for a well-integrity problem.

"Loud Alarms and Lights Tested?: No"

The same form records zero alarms or LAAs installed at this location (job description "Number of Alarms or LAAs: 0", checklist "Number of Alarms or LAAs: 00"), so the "No" is consistent with there having been no alarm present to test rather than with a test being skipped. Stop work / unsafe conditions — needs confirmation, not action

These are selections on the OWL multi-select, not confirmed events. Per Kelby Hammer's 09/23 guidance, technicians may be selecting "Unsafe conditions" because they regard wellhead work as inherently unsafe rather than because a specific condition arose. "Stop work authority utilized" was selected on no form today; every stop-work selection today was the routine "Stop work authority was discussed".
"Stop work authority was discussed" only (routine pre-job item, no action needed): Michael Jobe, Scarlet Unit 2, job 36242; Dawson Drake, TXL 27 Unit 3 2771JH, job 36185.
"Unsafe conditions" and "Stop work authority was discussed" together: Ruben Rojo, Elkin 21Y 25H, job 36229; Ruben Rojo, Meek Lindsay 6L 12H, job 36227; Dawson Drake, Brook N-13D 100H, job 36233.

Neither stop-work item selected: Rolando Flores on both Elkin (36230) and Meek Lindsay (36228); Robert Henigan on Scarlet (36243); and the four forms with entirely empty multi-selects listed under documentation below.

Not the mis-selection pattern — Ruben Rojo, both of his jobs. On Elkin 21Y 25H (36229) he selected "Unsafe conditions" with a one-word narrative, "Reconnect", and left the Learn section and "How did we leave this location better than we found it?" entirely blank. On Meek Lindsay 6L 12H (36227) he selected "Unsafe conditions" with the narrative "Disconnect and flange installation" and again left both close-out fields blank. With no positive close-out narrative to offset the selection, these follow the same shape as his 09/23/2026 form and should be treated as real until he confirms otherwise. Rojo is a repeat appearance on this list.

Dawson Drake's Brook N-13D form (36233) does fit the mis-selection pattern — "Unsafe conditions" selected, narrative "Reconnect", but the close-out is fully completed. Worth a word with him rather than an investigation.
Michael Jobe appeared on this list on 09/26/2026 for selecting "Unsafe conditions" twice with no supporting narrative. Today he did the opposite, which is reported as item 2 above.

The "What went well?" multi-select string is byte-identical across six forms today (Flores 36228 and 36230, Drake 36185 and 36233, Jobe 36242, and McCarter's 10/24 form), which indicates a selection being carried forward rather than made fresh. Rojo's two forms likewise share an identical observe list.

clean.text: Rolando Flores 1099 filed three Trailer Inspection Forms for trailer 606 and its Trailer Readiness Form, all with complete same-day photo sets and complete bottle entries, plus two air job forms with full narratives and completed Learn sections — the most complete set of the day. Robert Henigan 1099's Trailer Readiness Form for trailer 607 was the cleanest trailer form filed: all ten bottle positions recorded, every photo captured on 10/25, and "Is anything wrong or missing?" answered. Jordan Lemmons' two Trailer Inspection Forms for trailer 605 were complete and consistent. Larry Taylor's Cactus 139 rig up had every photo captured on the day and loud alarms recorded as tested. Kyle Williams' Commuting Journey Management Plan was complete and internally consistent. Justin Pack's daily was complete on every answer and field apart from the one stale loud alarm photo noted above.

Trailer forms of both kinds, and the equipment sections of the H2S daily, are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside images, not as text, so none of them were verified. Separately, this review ran at 11:00 PM Central, so any submission arriving later tonight or tomorrow morning for Sunday's work is not included; the usual next-morning sweep for late arrivals could not be run before this report was sent.

36 of 36 submissions read. The job board for 10/25/2026 was available and that day's board was used, from Blake Walton's 10:34 AM email; 44 manned board rows were checked for coverage across the two workbooks — 20 on the Permian Basin board and 24 on the ArkLaTex board — of which 25 were live assignments after removing rows marked ON STANDBY, DAYS OFF, WTX SUPPORT and mobilizing.
